title: Chipotle Raises Sales Outlook, Says Value Perception Is Improving
excerpt: CEO Scott Boatwright pointed to the best affordability scores in two years as Q2 revenue topped Wall Street estimates, though a cyclospora outbreak dented July traffic.
body:
• Chipotle raised its full-year same-store sales forecast to "low single-digit" growth from roughly flat, after Q2 comparable sales rose 2.2% — accelerating from 0.5% in Q1.
  • CEO Scott Boatwright said affordability scores hit their best level in about two years, driven by menu innovation, lower-priced items, and improved execution rather than discounting alone.
  • The cyclospora outbreak linked to iceberg lettuce shaved roughly 200 basis points off sales in the second half of July, even though Chipotle sources its lettuce from California, not Mexico.

Chipotle Mexican Grill delivered a second-quarter earnings beat on July 29 and lifted its annual sales guidance, sending shares surging nearly 14% the following day as investors bet the burrito chain's turnaround is gaining ground.

Revenue rose 9.3% year over year to $3.35 billion, edging past the $3.33 billion Wall Street consensus. Adjusted earnings came in at 33 cents per share, one cent ahead of forecasts and flat with the year-ago period. Comparable-restaurant sales climbed 2.2%, with a 1% uptick in transactions and a 1.2% gain in average check — a signal the chain is pulling in more customers, not just charging them more.

"Our affordability scores were better in Q2 than they've been in probably the past couple of years."

— Scott Boatwright, CEO, Chipotle Mexican Grill

Value Perception: The Bigger Battle

For much of the past two years, Chipotle has been on the defensive over two interlocking consumer gripes: rising prices and inconsistent portion sizes. A TikTok-fueled shrinkflation controversy in 2024 drew headlines, a Wells Fargo study exposed wildly inconsistent bowl weights, and Boatwright himself went viral earlier this year after telling customers to "just ask" for more food.

On the Q2 call, the CEO framed the progress differently — not as a portion fix, but as a broader value recalibration. Brand tracking data showed improved perceptions of value "across all income groups and age cohorts," he said. Lower-priced items introduced in December, including a $3.50 single chicken taco and a $3.82 high-protein cup of adobo chicken, have helped broaden accessibility without across-the-board discounting.

"Value isn't just about discounting and price point. It's about convenience. It's about execution. It's about menu innovation," Boatwright told analysts. "There's a host of things that the consumer is looking at to determine value."

Strong Quarter, Squeezed Margins

The top-line strength masked margin pressure. Restaurant-level operating margin fell to 25.2% from 27.4% a year earlier, squeezed by beef and freight inflation running at 3% to 3.5% and higher labor costs from wage increases and staffing tied to hospitality initiatives. Food, beverage, and packaging costs climbed to nearly 30% of revenue, up from 29%.

Boatwright made clear the company is absorbing the hit rather than passing it to customers. "It's something we have decided to invest in this consumer environment, to not pass those costs to consumers when they're having a tough time," he told Barron's.

The strategy appears to be working on one front: the chain's Matchday BOGO promotion set a single-day sales record, and its Honey Chicken limited-time offering achieved an attachment rate above 25%. Chipotle opened 100 restaurants during the quarter — 80 with drive-through Chipotlanes — and maintained its plan for 350 to 370 new locations this year, including forthcoming markets in Mexico City, Seoul, and Singapore.

Cyclospora Shadow

The quarter's momentum ran into a headwind in July. A cyclospora outbreak linked to shredded iceberg lettuce sourced from Mexico by produce giant Taylor Farms sickened thousands of Americans and triggered sweeping lettuce recalls. Chipotle's romaine lettuce comes from California and is not implicated, but the chain still took a hit.

Chief Financial Officer Adam Rymer said traffic softened by about 200 basis points in the second half of July. The company now expects third-quarter comparable sales growth of roughly 1%, assuming the drag persists through the period.

"News like this, to be quite honest, hurts everyone. This isn't an isolated event for one brand. We hate to see it."

— Scott Boatwright, CEO, Chipotle Mexican Grill

Some analysts believe the impact is overstated. William Blair analyst Sharon Zackfia wrote that the drag is unlikely to last through the full quarter, suggesting actual comparable sales could beat the 1% guidance.

What's Next

Chipotle plans two additional limited-time protein offerings in the second half of 2026, alongside experiments in beverages, sides, and desserts. Its High-Efficiency Equipment Package — now in more than 1,000 restaurants — is producing two to three extra entrees during peak 15-minute service windows, with a target of 2,000 locations by year-end. A frictionless in-store rewards pilot launching in August could lift rewards participation from about 20% of in-store transactions toward the nearly 90% rate its digital channel already achieves.

The second quarter suggests the top-line recovery is becoming more credible. The next test, as Barron's noted, is whether Chipotle can convert that momentum into stronger profits while holding the line on price.
